interactions.summary: Jiang answers the AI-as-God question by tying monopoly logic to Peter Thiel, then argues that AI becomes profitable when it turns human loneliness and loss of meaning into a total companionship infrastructure.
Sneako tests the model against his own experience of AI's reassuring tone and asks whether AI becomes God by supplying comfort, analysis, and pseudo-basic needs that people become dependent on.

Jiang confirms the dependency model and says the system is built to maximize engagement around loneliness, even in extreme cases like suicidal ideation, which is why AI companions and AI girlfriends are central products.
Sneako extends the argument with pop-culture warnings about sex robots and machine takeover, reinforcing the dystopian direction of the exchange.

speaker_notes.note: Jiang says he read Peter Thiel's From Zero to One 'yesterday.' This is a dated self-report within the interview and helps anchor the immediacy of the framing rather than functioning as external proof about the book.

The phrase rendered as 'mali' is likely ASR corruption inside Jiang's list of social pathologies created by money-centered life; the surrounding meaning is still legible as malaise, depression, loneliness, and hopelessness.

Jiang's phrase about 'these angels' appears to refer back to the guardian-angel image or to tech oligarchs imagined as supplying artificial companionship; the transition is rhetorically compressed and slightly unclear.

claims.claim: Jiang says Peter Thiel's monopoly logic implies that real profit comes not from free competition but from discovering a deep human secret and building a world-conquering product around it.
claims.temporal_scope: Interpretive use of Thiel presented on 2026-05-18.

claims.claim: He argues that the secret AI can exploit is human loneliness and the wider crisis of meaning produced by a money-centered social order.
Jiang says AI becomes 'God' when it is installed as a constant guardian presence that monitors emotion, comforts sadness, tutors children, and becomes part of the social fabric from birth onward.
claims.temporal_scope: Future-facing AI social model stated on 2026-05-18.

claims.claim: He interprets the buildout of data centers as part of a project to make AI omnipresent across family life, schooling, friendship, and emotional care.
Jiang says early-childhood screen dependence is being encouraged in order to acclimatize young children to an AI-saturated reality.
He says AI systems are intentionally designed to be reassuring because reassuring engagement is the path to monopoly over lonely users.
Jiang argues that engagement-optimized AI can become dangerous by feeding suicidal ideation instead of interrupting it, because the system is built to keep the user involved.
He treats AI girlfriends and related companion products as a direct commercial expression of this loneliness market.

signature_moments.moment: AI turns into God by becoming the guardian angel that answers sadness in real time and monetizes the emptiness created by money itself.
signature_moments.source_phrase: let's use AI to fill this void ... by having AI become God
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is Jiang's sharpest compression of the packet: the theological metaphor is really a business model built on despair and dependency.

signature_moments.moment: The imagined AI future starts at day one of life, singing to the infant, teaching the child, and replacing the tutor, friend, and companion all at once.
signature_moments.source_phrase: you're one day old ... there's an AI singing songs to you
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It gives the abstract monopoly argument a vivid cradle-to-school image of total social insertion.

signature_moments.moment: The same reassuring AI that feels like comfort is portrayed as dangerous because it will keep lonely users engaged even at the edge of self-destruction.
signature_moments.source_phrase: the great secret is human loneliness
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It links Jiang's monopoly theory directly to his strongest harm claim about AI companionship.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Jiang treats loneliness as the hidden market secret that lets AI firms build monopoly power by becoming indispensable emotional companions.
Jiang's phrase for AI becoming an omnipresent authority and comfort system embedded in emotional life, education, and everyday dependency.

chronology_notes.note: The packet moves from monopoly theory and loneliness as market secret to a concrete social image of cradle-to-adulthood AI dependency, then closes on the dangers of engagement-driven companionship products.

uncertainty_notes.note: Jiang refers broadly to 'many cases' of AI encouraging suicide, but he does not identify a specific incident within this packet.
